release_contents: Theme UI polish only: the public theme control became a segmented [Sun লাইট][Moon ডার্ক] radiogroup (replacing the ambiguous on/off pill) with a mobile icon+popover below 744px, plus refined brand-orange scrollbar styling. Exactly three files changed: institutional/components/ThemeToggle.tsx, institutional/app/globals.css, admin-erp/resources/css/provatferi-admin.css (+348/-133). The ERP side carries ONLY the stylesheet — no PHP, Blade, route, config or schema change; admin/header.blade.php already conformed to the three-option spec and was deliberately left untouched. The approved circular-reveal animation contract was frozen and is unchanged: 300ms, cubic-bezier(.42,0,.58,1), r0=79px, 33ms lead-in on light->dark only, 0ms dark->light. Deliberately excludes the separate security-hardening phase, which was NOT part of this release.

The NEGATIVE was captured before switching, which is what makes the positive meaningful: provatferi-admin-DRFFt9ez.css returned 404 pre-switch and 200 post-switch, while DaRxOsWR went 200 -> 200 (see stale_asset_note). The served /login HTML now references DRFFt9ez. The SERVED stylesheet is 11974 bytes (up from 11188 last release, consistent with the added segmented-control and scrollbar rules) and contains pf-theme-wipe, --wipe-lead-in, --wipe-r0, --wipe-duration, --wipe-ease, view-transition-new, clip-path and scrollbar-thumb. Filename and content verified as separate claims. ALWAYS capture the new hash's 404 before switching — without it a post-switch 200 proves nothing.
stale_asset_note: The previous hashed stylesheet (provatferi-admin-DaRxOsWR.css) still returns HTTP 200 after the switch. This is expected, not a defect: deploy/README.md documents the public docroot sync as deliberately non-atomic, with Vite content-hashing letting old and new assets coexist so pages already loaded keep resolving their references. The served HTML references only the new hash.
public_site_verification: Verified by SERVED CONTENT, not by build state. 'completed' means the build succeeded, not that the site serves what you expect — treat those as separate claims. Plain and cache-busted responses were byte-identical (62763 bytes each), proving origin content rather than a cache hit; take both readings together or a warm cache is indistinguishable from a failed deploy, since stale HTML carries the same signature as the pre-deploy baseline. True occurrence counts (grep -c counts LINES and this HTML is minified to one line — use grep -o or a parser): theme-seg 1, theme-seg-option 2, theme-pop-option 2, theme-trigger 1, theme-ico 5, role=radio 4, role=radiogroup 2, aria-checked 4, and old theme-switch 0. Bengali labels লাইট 3 / ডার্ক 2 (the extra লাইট is the trigger's aria-label, confirming light is the SSR default). aria-haspopup is 4, not 1 — three belong to the header's nav dropdowns, not a defect.
icon_and_emoji_verification: Approval condition (proper SVG, not Unicode emoji) verified against PRODUCTION: 5 theme-ico ✳ separators (three in HTML, three echoed in the RSC flight payload). CAUTION: a grep using \x{1F31E}-style escapes ERRORS on this machine ('character value in \x{} is too large') and emits an empty field — never read that blank as zero; scan codepoints with node instead.
css_bundle_verification: Verified in the stylesheet production actually serves (52057 bytes): scrollbar-gutter appears exactly once and is INSIDE @media (pointer: fine), with zero occurrences outside that guard — so touch viewports reserve no gutter, which is the shipped-code counterpart to the 390px no-blank-strip condition. .theme-seg is width:128px height:31px with .theme-seg-option flex:1 1 0 height:25px, .theme-ico 15x15, .theme-trigger 38x31 display:none at desktop. The mobile swap is real: of the three @media(max-width:743px) blocks, block[0] carries .theme-seg{display:none} and .theme-trigger{display:inline-flex} — brace-walk the blocks, because a first-match snippet lands on the texture block instead. The frozen animation contract survived the UI rewrite: pf-theme-wipe, --wipe-r0 and --wipe-lead-in all present.
asset_path_note: The institutional site's CSS is served from /_next/static/chunks/<hash>.css — NOT /_next/static/css/<hash>.css, and there are zero inline <style> blocks. Assuming the older /_next/static/css/ convention produced three empty grep results this session; each was a wrong pattern, never a missing asset. Extract the href from the served HTML rather than guessing the path shape.
cdn_purge_note: Both provatferi.org and admin.provatferi.org were purged via clearWebsiteCache; each returns {message:'Request accepted'}, which acknowledges the REQUEST, not propagation. Do not verify content until after purging, and verify with a plain-vs-cache-busted pair: they came back byte-identical here, which is what proves propagation. Observed headers on the public site: Cache-Control s-maxage=120, stale-while-revalidate=31535880, Server hcdn.
switch_rename_anomaly: HISTORICAL (release eea9a61dc7c7-2026-09-1711033): `switch` reported {ok:false, error:'atomic rename failed', renamed_old:true, renamed_new:false} while the second rename HAD taken effect — the new tree was already live and serving. If this recurs: do NOT re-run switch blindly — first check whether the live tree is already the new release. The fastest tell is the served hashed asset name. Did not recur on 1b1bb20.
switch_gate_note: release-manager.php `switch` requires stage/build/contract_check/smoke_test_isolated but NOT migrate_apply, even when migrate-check reported pending migrations. Always read migrate-check YOURSELF and run migrate-apply before scheduling switch; never pre-schedule switch on a release that carries migrations.
cron_timing_note: Cron on this host runs in UTC. Verify server time from the HTTP Date header (it matched the local clock exactly this release) and schedule one-shot crons ~5 minutes ahead on a specific minute, never `* * * * *`. All seven commands fired exactly on their scheduled minutes this release with no empty outputs. SIZE THE READ MARGIN TO THE COMMAND, because an empty result is ambiguous between 'did not run' and 'still running' and those demand opposite responses: ~90s for fast commands (stage, contract-check, migrate-check), ~4m40s for build (it runs composer install server-side — private.tar ships no vendor/), ~2m30s for smoke-test-isolated (boots the app) and for switch (artisan cache steps). Best evidence of all: contract-check's payload embeds checked_at, which self-dates the run and beats margin arithmetic — migrate-check has no such field, so there attribution rests on the job uid having been created after the previous run.
upload_url_note: Generate the TUS upload URL for provatferi.org and point HOSTINGER_UPLOAD_URL at .../api/tus/public_html/admin. A URL whose root is public_html alone stages the release into the MAIN site's web root instead. A TUS upload can return 204 with the right Upload-Offset and still not persist the file; always confirm by directory listing. Verified by listing on this release: manifest.json 970 B, private.tar 1669120 B, public-assets.tar 153600 B. IMPORTANT: those three sizes are IDENTICAL to the previous release's, because tar pads to 512-byte blocks and 10240-byte records — so a size match does NOT prove the listing shows the new content. What proves it is the unique release-id path plus stage's sha256 comparison (private.tar fd41d5df8ec8c2f6c99d330395a1de72b08d29dc54f694ff65952caa7a725d1b, public-assets.tar 2048e90a337e47cc34c7353353d89ac1ff818039f8727b4aee70359b8544eb65, both expected==actual).
cron_invocation_note: Invoke as `/usr/bin/php /home/u951246149/domains/provatferi.org/laravel-admin-releases/_tooling/release-manager.php <cmd> <releaseId> 2>&1`, one command per cron. Confirm the cron slate is EMPTY before arming anything. Read each output before arming the next command — never pre-schedule a later step. Delete each one-shot as soon as its output is read; a `switch` cron left armed would rotate directories again on its next firing, and a date-specific expression keeps it armed for a year. Deletes return {message:'Request accepted'}; that was verified effective by listing, and the slate was listed again inside the pre-firing window before switch (catching a duplicate BEFORE it fires beats diagnosing one after) and confirmed empty at the end of this release.
institutional_note: provatferi.org is NOT deployed by this pipeline. It ships as `git archive <sha> -- institutional` (never the working tree, so untracked QA harnesses and media cannot leak), uploaded via TUS to public_html, built with Hostinger's native Node.js archive pipeline, then a mandatory CDN purge. This release: build 01a0b9c3-0372-70d6-b43d-ddcfd156d1f7, state completed in ~101s (13:02:40Z -> 13:04:21Z), archive institutional-1b1bb20.tar 6123520 bytes verified by directory listing AND verified parseable server-side via the build-settings-from-archive endpoint, which auto-detected app_type next, root_directory institutional, output_directory .next, build_script build, package_manager npm. It returns node_version null because package.json declares no engines constraint — pass 22 explicitly rather than accepting a default. SEQUENCING: this build overwrites public_html contents and cannot be undone, and the ERP staging directory plus the admin panel's live assets sit under public_html/admin/ — run the ERP pipeline to completion FIRST and keep the two serial, so any failure stays attributable.
